questions.template: Skeletons do three jobs. Which one is a skeleton job?
questions.hint: Without it you'd be a puddle of wobble.
questions.explain: Skeletons give support, protection, and movement — support keeps you standing tall.

questions.hint: It's a bony helmet you were born wearing.
questions.explain: The skull is a built-in helmet protecting your brilliant brain.

questions.hint: It's a bony cage around your chest.
questions.explain: The ribcage guards your heart and lungs like a fence of bone.

questions.template: What is another name for your backbone?
questions.explain: The spine is the chain of bones down your back — it holds you up!

questions.template: Muscles work in pairs. When one muscle pulls, what does its partner do?
questions.hint: Like a see-saw: one side works, one side rests.
questions.explain: Muscle pairs take turns: one contracts (pulls) while the other relaxes.

choices: Yes — pushing is all they do
questions.hint: That's WHY they need a partner!
questions.explain: Muscles only pull — that's exactly why they work in pairs, one on each side.

questions.template: Animals with a skeleton INSIDE their body are called…?
questions.hint: It comes from the word for backbone: vertebra.
questions.explain: Vertebrates have backbones inside — like Max, Digger, and you!

questions.template: A snail has a shell. What kind of skeleton is that?
questions.explain: Shells and insect armour are exoskeletons — support and protection worn on the outside.

questions.template: Why do bigger animals usually need thicker leg bones?
questions.hint: Think of table legs holding a heavy table.
questions.explain: Support scales with weight — heavy bodies need strong, thick columns of bone.
